Triage: duplicate reports

owner j3apyye proposed reviewed 2026-11-04 · 0 days ago

A busy morning brings hundreds of reports about the same thing. We keep one ticket per issue and merge every duplicate into it, so engineering sees one thread with a count.

The rule

This proposed revision follows decision 0002. The original accepted decision 0001 is preserved as history; the export cannot establish adoption by the live desk.

  1. Read the report body and identify the tenant, channel and relevant form version.
  2. Use the tenant’s locale and the executable cause rule to identify candidate tickets.
  3. Check that the symptoms support the candidate cause. Subject similarity helps find candidates; it is not the merge criterion.
  4. Merge evidence of the same cause and retain each report ID. Keep different causes apart, even when the subjects match. Count distinct report IDs once.
The explorer shows that matching subjects can have different modeled causes, and different subjects can share a cause. Its classifier does not read bodies; contradictory symptoms still need investigation. See the [#4471 review](/kb/incidents/4471-review).

When you are unsure

Keep the report separate pending investigation. An unknown tenant or a different symptom does not establish a duplicate. Ask for the original entered date, stored timestamp, timezone, invite payload and reproduction steps. Record the unresolved report IDs so a queued fix does not hide them. Recompute the page’s counts after a fresh export.

For a report arriving after the reported fix or form retirement, check whether the relevant product path still exists and whether the reported fix applies. Do not merge automatically into a closed ticket. The supplied classifier describes this export’s routing model; it is not proof of the cause of a new failure.
